Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that’s all from this entertaining contest. Pakistan take a 1-0 lead in the series and will look to wrap it up in the next game, while Sri Lanka will be eager to bounce back and take it to a decider. The action resumes here in Rawalpindi for the 2nd ODI on 13th November, Thursday, starting at 9.30 am GMT. Do join us early for all the build-up and pre-match excitement. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Shaheen Afridi, the victorious skipper of Pakistan, says that he is happy with the performance of his team. He continues by praising the partnership between Salman Agha and Hussain Talat. He adds that it's because of them that they were able to put a target of 300 on the board. Mentions that they should minimise the dot ball percentage in the Powerplay in their batting inning. Also credits Haris Rauf and reckons that Rauf is a natural wicket-taker for their side. Ends up saying that it was an awesome catch by Babar Azam at the slips.

Charith Asalanka, the captain of Sri Lanka, says that they bowled really well in the first 20 overs or so. Adds that after that, they were a bit inconsistent but credits Salman and Talat for the way they batted. Mentions that they conceded a few too many, as he thought they could have restricted Pakistan to 260-270, as this was not a 300 wicket. Says that, including him, a few of the batters made some bad decisions, and they lost a lot of wickets in the middle, but Rauf also bowled very well at the same time. Ends by saying that Wanindu Hasaranga is a key player for him and he has been contributing with both bat and ball, and hopes that he continues to do so for the team.

Salman Agha is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his superb hundred. He says that he played one ball at a time, and that is the reason he succeeded in scoring big runs. He also reckons that his partnership with him and Hussain Talat was important for his team. He also adds that running between the wickets was the main highlight of their partnership, as they kept on with their singles and doubles to keep the scoreboard ticking. Ends up saying that he knew that they could score 100 runs in the last 10 overs, as they have finishers like Mohammad Nawaz, so they just tried to take the game deep, and it worked.
Presentation Time...

Pakistan’s new-ball duo, Shaheen Afridi and Naseem Shah, struggled to find their rhythm early on, conceding plenty of runs and extras that made life easy for the batters. It was also the fourth straight game where they failed to take a wicket in the first Powerplay. However, Haris Rauf turned things around brilliantly, striking three times in back-to-back overs to bring Pakistan right back into the contest. He later broke a threatening stand as well, aided by a superb catch from Babar Azam. Naseem Shah had a rough outing but finished strongly with a couple of key wickets, including the big one of Hasaranga, while Faheem Ashraf and Mohammad Nawaz chipped in with crucial strikes to help Pakistan just edge over the line. Still, there are a few areas they’ll want to tidy up before the next match.

Earlier in the game, Pakistan put up an impressive total, though it wasn’t all smooth going early on. The top order struggled to get going, but Salman Agha once again stood tall with a superb unbeaten 107 off 87 balls. He found a reliable partner in Hussain Talat, who notched up his maiden ODI fifty, and the pair added a vital 138-run stand to steady the innings. Mohammad Nawaz then provided the late flourish to take the score close to 300. For Sri Lanka, Wanindu Hasaranga was the standout with three wickets, while Maheesh Theekshana and Asitha Fernando took one each, but they’ll rue the missed LBW on Talat at 95 for 4 - a moment that proved decisive once their reviews were gone.

Skipper Charith Asalanka, after surviving an early chance, combined well with Sadeera Samarawickrama to steady the innings with a solid 57-run stand, but Babar Azam produced a stunning catch at first slip to swing the momentum back Pakistan’s way. Asalanka and Janith Liyanage kept the chase alive with smart rotation and timely boundaries, but a rush of blood saw the skipper throw his wicket away, leaving the visitors under pressure. Liyanage soon fell to a peach from Naseem Shah, and with Kamindu Mendis failing to make an impact, it looked doomed for the Lankans. However, Wanindu Hasaranga was not going to go down without a fight and batted superbly to keep them alive in the chase, scoring an excellent fifty, but he fell for 59 at the wrong time with them still needing 21 runs. Maheesh Theekshana's couple of lusty blows got them within touching distance, but they ultimately fell short by just 6 runs.

Sri Lanka got off to a flying start, capitalizing on some erratic bowling from Pakistan and positive intent from Pathum Nissanka and debutant Kamil Mishara, who looked in fine touch. The pair added 85 runs for the opening stand, putting the visitors in control early on. However, once the field restrictions were lifted, things quickly unraveled - both openers fell soon after, and with Kusal Mendis departing for a golden duck, Sri Lanka suddenly slipped from 85 for 0 to 90 for 3, finding themselves needing to rebuild all over again.

A thriller to kick off the ODI series in Pindi! Pakistan draw first blood, but they had to fight hard to cross the finish line. In a game that swung both ways, the hosts just held their nerve better in the crunch moments. Cricket can be cruel at times - Wanindu Hasaranga’s all-round brilliance nearly pulled off a famous win for Sri Lanka, but in the end, it was a case of so close, yet so far.

Not the ending Sri Lanka hoped to get, but kudos to the lower middle order for staying in the game! A slower delivery to end the inning, on middle. Maheesh Theekshana punches it hard just toward the right of the bowler. Talat looks to hop and take the catch but fails to get any hands on it. The ball rolls toward long on and the batter gets a brace. Pakistan win the encounter by 6 runs and take a 1-0 lead in the series.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Excellent shot! Short of a length and wide outside off, Kamil Mishara gets the chance to free his arms and crunches it through point for his first boundary in ODIs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Naseem Shah to Kamil Mishara, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Pulls his length back a bit, on off, Kamil Mishara stabs it out to extra cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Naseem Shah to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full again and shaping into leg, Kamil Mishara fails to work it away but this time the ball brushes the pads before going to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Naseem Shah to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up and on middle, Kamil Mishara drills it straight back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Naseem Shah to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Another extra! Goes fuller but shaping down the leg side, Kamil Mishara fails to glance it away. The umpire signals a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Naseem Shah to Kamil Mishara, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on off, Pathum Nissanka dabs it towards point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Naseem Shah to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on middle, Pathum Nissanka nudges it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Naseem Shah to Pathum Nissanka, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FIVE WIDES! Not sure what is happening with Pakistani pacers, but they are not able to control their lines. Naseem Shah spills this full but way, way down the leg side, Pathum Nissanka lets it go. Rizwan once again has no chance of stopping that as it trickles away to the fine leg fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Naseem Shah to Pathum Nissanka, 5 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: EDGED AND DROPPED! Proves that Salman Agha is human after all. Shaheen Afridi lands this on a good length, in the channel outside off, holds its line. Pathum Nissanka pushes hard at it but gets an outside edge straight to first slip. Agha tries to grab it with both hands around his waist but the ball bursts through his hands. Nissanka gets a life now!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and outside off, anglig away again, Pathum Nissanka tries to cut it away but gets beaten due to the extra bounce.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length and around off, takes pace off, angling it away as well, Pathum Nissanka offers not shot at it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Shaheen Afridi has to reload that one! He lands this back of a length, but way outside off, Pathum Nissanka lets it go. Another wide!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Good length and on off, Pathum Nissanka stays back and taps it out to the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nicely bowled! Shaheen Afridi nails the yorker now, on off, swings in a bit in the air, Pathum Nissanka gets his bat down in time to dig it out well.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on off, Pathum Nissanka drills it to the right of the mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FIVE WIDES! Too many extras already from Pakistan! Shaheen Afridi goes fuller but on the leg stump line, shaping it further in. Pathum Nissanka fails to flick it away, and Mohammad Rizwan has no chance of stopping that even with a dive to his left, as the ball races to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, 5 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: The stumps save a couple of runs here! Pitched up and on middle, Kamil Mishara plays a delightful straight drive past the bowler. Howerver, he has hit it a bit too straight and the ball hits the wickets at the non-striker's end and rolls away towards the mid-wicket region. The batters get two runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Naseem Shah to Kamil Mishara, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the length hard and on off, Kamil Mishara gets on top of it and slaps it through covers for a brace.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Naseem Shah to Kamil Mishara, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on off, Kamil Mishara gets on his toes and punches it sweetly but straight to short cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Naseem Shah to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Touch fuller and around off, Pathum Nissanka plays the square drive through backward point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Naseem Shah to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Much better! Good length and on middle, Pathum Nissanka gets behind the line of it and blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Naseem Shah to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Easy pickings! Naseem Shah has yet to find his rhythm here! He lands this back of a length, angling into the leg side. Pathum Nissanka glances it away to the deep fine leg fence for an easy boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Naseem Shah to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Goes fuller but this time well outside off, shaping it away. Pathum Nissanka lets it go. Another wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Naseem Shah to Pathum Nissanka, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Naseem Shah errs in his line and begins with a short delivery down the leg side, Pathum Nissanka tries to hook it away but misses. Wided.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Naseem Shah to Pathum Nissanka, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Who will operate from the other end? Naseem Shah it is!
Hard length and on off, Pathum Nissanka runs it down to third man for one. 5 runs off the first over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Bangs this into the pitch, but well outside off, angling further away. Pathum Nissanka fails to reach out for it. Wided.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the length hard and around off, Pathum Nissanka punches it to extra cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: First runs off the bat! Short of a length and on off, Kamil Mishara steers it through point for a single. He wants the second but is sent back, and rightly so. Mishara gets off the mark in his ODI career.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Shaheen Afridi to Kamil Mishara, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on middle, Kamil Mishara stays back and pats it to short mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Shaheen Afridi to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good-length delivery, in the channel outside off, holds its line, Kamil Mishara watches it through and leaves it alone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Shaheen Afridi to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: TWO WIDES! Sri Lanka are underway with extras! Shaheen Afridi loses his line and serves this full, way down the leg side. Pathum Nissanka lets it go and Mohammad Rizwan, the keeper, dives to his left but fails to collect it cleanly. It is called a wide and bye is taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, 2 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: Shaheen Afridi starts with a back-of-a-length delivery, outside off, angling it away. Pathum Nissanka slashes hard at it but fails to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Shaheen Afridi to Pathum Nissanka, No run.
